title: Lesson Plan — Grassroots Democracy: Governance (Class 6 CBSE Social Science)
subject: Social Science
objectives: Define governance and list the pillars of good governance.
Explain what democracy is and identify its key features.
State the key dates and words of the Indian Republic (1947, 1950, Sovereign / Secular / Republic).
Identify the three levels of Indian government and which subjects each handles.
Explain the role of local government and the 73rd/74th Amendments.
List ways a citizen can participate in democracy beyond voting.
prerequisites: Familiarity with the words 'rule', 'leader', 'election' from earlier classes.
A basic sense of what a 'country', 'state' and 'village' are.
materials: A printed Indian Constitution Preamble (one per group)
Cards with subject names: 'foreign affairs', 'village well', 'state police', 'currency'
Three boxes labelled UNION, STATE, LOCAL

activities.description: Hook: 'Suppose your village's well is broken. Who fixes it — the Prime Minister, your state Chief Minister, or your village Panchayat? Why?' Take guesses; promise the chapter answers.

Subject-sorting game. Students sort the cards (foreign affairs, village well, state police, currency, school maintenance, defence, sanitation) into the three boxes UNION / STATE / LOCAL. Discuss why each fits where it does.
student_actions: Justify each placement to the class.

activities.description: Cover four blocks: (i) governance + 3 pillars; (ii) democracy + 5 features + Greek roots; (iii) Indian Republic — the Preamble's five big words, and the dates 1947 / 1950; (iv) three levels + 73rd/74th Amendment / Gram Swaraj.
teacher_actions: Write the Preamble on the board.
Define each Preamble word in simple language.
Drill the three levels and which subject each handles.
Tell the story of the 1992 Amendments.
student_actions: Repeat: Sovereign / Socialist / Secular / Democratic / Republic.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions on definitions, levels, Preamble words and a short reading on a fictional gram-sabha meeting.
Exit ticket: 4 quick questions, one from each block.
Homework: ask a parent or older neighbour about the last election they voted in — what level of government was it (local / state / Lok Sabha)? Bring back one fact.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (Local Government — Rural).

homework: Find out who is your local Panchayat or Municipal ward representative.
List two Fundamental Rights and two Fundamental Duties from the Constitution.
Write 4–5 lines on why the local well in your area is best fixed by the local government, not by the Prime Minister.
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz at the start of next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on Gram Swaraj with the rubric in the answer key.
Peer-grade the homework on local representative.
references: NCERT Class 6 Social Science — Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Chapter 10: Grassroots Democracy — Part 1: Governance.
